data.name: Sangeeta
data.long_meaning: Sangeeta is a Sanskrit name derived from the Sanskrit word ‘sang’ meaning ‘together’ and ‘geeta’ meaning ‘song’ or ‘melody’. In Hindu mythology, Sangeeta is the goddess of music and is considered to be the source of all musical melodies. This name is believed to inspire creativity, harmony, and a deep appreciation for the arts.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sangeeta carries rich cultural significance as it represents the traditional essence of India's vibrant musical heritage. The name is synonymous with the role of music in every aspect of Indian life, from religious rituals and social gatherings, to art, literature, and personal creativity. The influence of this name extends beyond borders, inspiring a sense of reverence and appreciation for music and its role in enriching human experiences.
data.spiritual_significance: Sangeeta is a name deeply rooted in spiritual symbolism, representing the transformative power of music. Hindu mythology holds that the world was created through the vibrations of sound, and music is believed to have the power to inspire self-realization and connect individuals to the Divine. The name Sangeeta is therefore believed to bring spiritual growth, creativity, and a deeper understanding of the world around us. It is a reminder of the power of the arts to elevate the human spirit and foster a sense of harmony and peace within.

historical_references.reference: Sangeeta is believed to be the name of the celestial singer in Hindu mythology who created the melodies of the universe. This divine musician is said to play the veena, a traditional Indian stringed instrument, and is often depicted alongside Lord Saraswati, the goddess of knowledge and music.

In medieval India, Sangeeta was also used as a title for royal women who were skilled in music and dance. These women were trained from a young age and served as courtesans and entertainers for the royal households.
